moneyline_market.question: Who will win ARI vs LAC scheduled for September 13, 2026 at 20:25 UTC?
moneyline_market.rules_digest: Settles to the winner; overtime is included if played; a tie pays 0.50; if delayed, postponed, or suspended and not rescheduled to a date within two days of the original date, it resolves at last fair market price; the relevant governing body determines the outcome.

comparison.reason: Both records identify the Arizona Cardinals versus Los Angeles Chargers NFL game scheduled September 13, 2026.
ARI/Arizona/Cardinals and LAC/Los Angeles C/Chargers map consistently.
Both contract records identify September 13, 2026.
Polymarket US states 20:25 UTC; the Kalshi contract text states the date but not kickoff time. Kalshi occurrence_datetime is not treated as kickoff evidence.
Both use the governing body's official game winner for ordinary completion.
Polymarket US expressly includes overtime if played; the observed Kalshi contract rules do not state overtime treatment separately.
Both observed contract rules pay 0.50 to each team outcome on a tie.
Polymarket US guidance specifies last fair market price; the observed Kalshi contract rules do not explicitly address no contest.

Kalshi requires the game to begin within 48 hours of the original start; Polymarket US target text conditions fair-market settlement on whether the game is rescheduled to a date within two days. These are not the same trigger.
The observed Kalshi child rules do not fully specify cancellation, abandonment, or suspended-game treatment comparable to the Polymarket US sports guidance.
Polymarket US guidance describes official review and replay handling; equivalent Kalshi target-specific handling was not observed.
Both primarily defer to the relevant governing league/body for the game result.
Kalshi names NFL.com; Polymarket US target metadata has no specific resolutionSource and its general guidance contains fallback sources.
Kalshi latest expiration is 2026-09-15T20:25:00Z; the Polymarket US moneyline end time is 2026-09-27T20:25:00Z.
The observed fields do not establish equivalent final settlement timing across all ordinary and exceptional states.
Both use fair-market settlement in some exceptional states, but the triggering conditions and expiration windows differ materially.
Equivalent reopening behavior was not established from the target-specific records.
This is one game with two team-winner outcomes; a tie is handled by a stated 0.50 payout rather than multiple winners.
Arizona and Chargers winner outcomes span normal official game-winner results.
Different postponement triggers and expiration windows can cause different exceptional-state settlement values.

outcome_mapping.kalshi_payoff: YES when Los Angeles Chargers wins
outcome_mapping.polymarket_us_payoff: Chargers side when Los Angeles Chargers wins

decision_reason: Explicit material mismatches in postponement/rescheduling triggers, expiration windows, and resulting exceptional-state fair-market treatment prevent economic equivalence. Additional material fields remain UNKNOWN and were not promoted to MATCH.
